_comment: Consensus Edge parameters, v1.
PROVENANCE OF EVERY NUMBER IN THIS FILE, because the difference
matters more than the values themselves:
measured  - derived from an out-of-sample result committed under
docs/measurements/. Quote these.
prior     - a starting value chosen for a stated reason, never
validated. Do NOT quote these as findings.
The composite weights are MIXED, and each one says which it is.
Market Mispricing has an out-of-sample result and it is a NULL:
rho +0.040 (7d, 12 folds) and +0.031 (14d, 6 folds), with the
market-value benchmark - a plain 'buy cheap players' rule - beating
it in 9 of 12 and 5 of 6. The earlier +0.089/+0.126/+0.111 was
measured on a board that priced every IDP row on a scale that does
not exist; see ADR-021. Its 0.5 is now a PRIOR like the others: the
only component with any signal was the one whose signal came from
the defect.
Opportunity has one too, and it is a NULL - see its weight
below. Sharp Flow has none, and the reason is worse than the one
recorded here before 2026-08-04. That reason - the qualified cohort
is recomputed live per request with no as-of concept anywhere in
src/sharp/ - is true and is a blocker, but fixing it would not be
enough. The movement corpus is itself conditioned on TODAY's
cohort: scripts/crawl_sharp_activity.py visits only currently-
qualified managers, so a manager qualified at a past date but not
now had their movements never collected. That is survivorship on a
proxy for the outcome, it is upstream of every filter, and no
as-of cohort can recover data that was never gathered. A historical
Sharp Flow backtest is therefore unsound at any budget; the only
sound route is forward-only, which the daily snapshot store already
accrues one observation per day.
Its 0.3 is therefore still a declared prior and is moot in every
reachable environment, where the ledger is empty.
This is why the consensus_edge feature flag defaults OFF and why
components are reported separately in every payload. The flag was
ON for part of 2026-08-04 and was returned to OFF by the same
pre-registered gate that had passed it - see ADR-023.
Do not edit in place once a paramSetId has shipped values - the id
is a content hash, so any edit produces a new id and stored results
stay attributable to the params that produced them.

_rationale: Mispricing carries the most weight because it is the only
component that computes at all in a reachable environment, NOT
because it is validated - it was, and on the scale-repaired board
it is not (see the provenance block). Sharp Flow is second
because qualified-manager behaviour is genuinely independent
evidence when it exists, which outside production it does not.
Neither 0.5 nor 0.3 is a fitted number and neither should be
quoted as one.
Opportunity is ZERO because it was measured and did not earn a
weight. It was believed unbacktestable - rank_history.jsonl is
untracked and always has been - until the panel turned out to
reconstruct board history from committed payloads and CSVs, which
is the same series that file records. Measured that way, adding
the board-momentum axis LOWERED mean rho at both powered
horizons and beat mispricing alone in a minority of folds. The
bar was set before the number was known: beat the validated
component out of sample or carry no weight.
The axis still computes and is still shown per row - the evidence
is real and a user can read it. It simply does not move the
score, and score.py::composite excludes zero-weight components
from componentsPresent so it cannot inflate confidence either.
Weights are renormalised over PRESENT components only, so a
player with no sharp data is not silently scored as though sharp
evidence were neutral - see score.py::composite.

_weightProvenance.mispricing: measured NULL - docs/measurements/consensus-edge-backtest-2026-08-04-h14.json; the 0.5 is a prior
_weightProvenance.sharpFlow: prior - an as-of cohort in src/sharp/ is necessary but NOT sufficient; the movement corpus is itself survivorship-biased upstream (scripts/crawl_sharp_activity.py crawls only currently-qualified managers), which no as-of filter can undo

_rationale: Bands are symmetric and round. They are NOT calibrated: with a
single validated component there is no basis for asserting that
+60 means anything different in kind from +55. They exist to make
the score readable, and the UI labels them experimental.
A score near zero has two completely different meanings: nothing
is happening, or strong evidence is cancelling. Averaging them to
the same number is the single most misleading thing a composite
can do, so opposing components above this magnitude force the
Conflicted label regardless of the arithmetic.
Beta(1,1) is a uniform prior: with no observations the posterior
mean is 0.5, i.e. direction 0.0, which is the honest answer.
The recency half-life and the caps address defects measured on
main: today's signal applies no per-manager or per-league cap at
all, so one active manager in ten leagues contributes ten
observations. maxManagerShare/maxLeagueShare bound any single
contributor's influence on one asset.
A geometric mean, so a single zeroed factor collapses the whole
score. That is deliberate: confidence is a conjunction - fresh
data AND adequate coverage AND agreement - and an arithmetic mean
would let three strong factors hide one absent one.
